Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

against my better judgment phrase

also against one’s better judgment, against my will, against the grain, reluctantly

classical

Tac. Dial. 13.5: necessitāte cotīdiē aliquid contrā animum faciendī
Sen. Const. 19.2: aliquid contrā animum audiendī (Lewis & Short s.v. contrā)

contrā animum

contrā, preposition with the accusative; mostly with facere

against one’s inclination

“Against one’s liking”: doing what one would rather not, which is near “against my will” and “against the grain”. Neither this nor Traupman’s phrase says exactly “against what I think wise”.

Other words

  • adversum ingenium meum — against my nature

    adversum, preposition with the accusative · also used · modern · Traupman 101; Traupman 335

    Traupman’s phrase; not in Lewis & Short or the loci collections. It says “against my character” rather than “against what I think wise”.

  • invītā Minervā — against one’s natural bent

    ablative absolute: “Minerva being unwilling” · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.110: invītā Minervā, id est adversante et repugnante nātūrā (Lewis & Short), s.v. invītus; Hor. AP 385 (Lewis & Short)

    Doing what one has no gift for, not acting against one’s judgment; for “against my will”, mē invītō.

SourcesLewis & Short: adversus · Lewis & Short: ingenium · Lewis & Short: invitus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 101, 335.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
